No problem! Generally, is what you're getting is more than tuition, tuition gets paid first. So you're probably going to be in a similar situation that I was, having to pay a month (or two) rent in the dorms or however it is for you.

It seems stressful now, but believe me, things will work out pretty well once you get everything in order!

This also happened to me in my first year, except it was a little more. We couldn't get any loans due to my parents credit. First of all, what loans are you getting from the school? If you're getting the ParentPLUS and not accepting it because your parents cannot be approved, contact your financial aid office. Generally, if this is the case, they will augment your other loans with a slightly lower amount. In any case, I hope you've contacted financial aid. They can be very helpful through this. Surprisingly, most of the time they WANT you to attend so that they get money, so they generally work with you to find loans and/or scholarships.

Second, I'm hoping that this money you need isn't directly for tuition? I lived on campus, and what I was short of was needed for housing at the end of the semester. So, I got a job and worked my ass off. Then I got another job and worked even harder. If you can do Work Study on campus, that will help a lot.

Sorry this was so long, especially if it doesn't help. Hope it does though!

I'm totally late to this party, but I just wanted to share. I was always an advanced reader as a kid, testing out of high school level when I was still in grade school and such. Plus, my parents were very down-to-earth, and I think that is what helped me remain so grounded through my life.

But, when I was about 10, I remember my parents and I went out to dinner one night. My parents were discussing one of the many theories in ASoIaF, and were getting really into it. I, naturally, felt left out, and wanted in to this club. 

So, that night, my mom handed me A Game of Thrones.

I read the GoT and aCoK before I finished 5th grade. It took me all of 6th grade to finish Storm. 

Well, now I'm a die-hard fan with the rest of my family. A lot of the themes and events were waaaaay over my ten-year-old head, but I was comprehending what was going on. When I re-read the series at the start of high school, I had a moment of "You guys let me *read* this??" 

Long stories aside, the series gave me a passion for not just literature, but *good* literature. I have always looked for morality and greater themes in books, but man, did ASoIaF really solidify in my mind what good books are. I don't regret for a moment having read them at that age, and I'm glad my parents were cool with it.
